title: DOM events and Lightning Message Service
summary: Choose a communication contract for related components and for independent regions of the same Lightning application.
prerequisites: M21 lifecycle and M22 data ownership.
JavaScript events and component public inputs.
learningObjectives: Use public properties down and events up a component tree.
Use LMS for appropriate cross-DOM communication.

sections.heading: Understand the mechanism
body: A child component should not reach into its parent's internal state. It can receive input through @api and announce an interaction through a DOM CustomEvent. The parent handles that event and decides what to do. This makes the child reusable: a visit row can announce a selected record without knowing whether the parent opens a panel, navigates, or updates a filter.

Lightning Message Service communicates across supported component regions in a Lightning page or application. It can connect components without a convenient common parent, including supported Aura or Visualforce integration points. A message channel defines the shared contract. LMS is a client-side application communication mechanism, not the server event bus used by Platform Events.

Keep messages small and meaningful. A selection message needs a recordId and perhaps an event type, not the entire customer record or a mutable object owned by another component. A subscriber should read current data through its authorized data source. Treat received IDs as input rather than proof that the user is allowed to access the record.

Choose subscription scope deliberately. Application-wide scope can deliver messages beyond the currently active region, which may be useful for a utility but surprising for a cached workspace component. Understand the component's lifetime, avoid duplicate subscriptions, and release resources appropriately. A hidden or cached component is not always equivalent to a destroyed component.

callouts.text: Use the narrowest communication boundary that matches the relationship between components.

sections.heading: Northstar Motors worked example
body: A Test Drive list contains individual row components. Each row dispatches visitselect with its ID; the list's parent manages selectedId and passes it into the detail component. No message service is necessary for that ordinary tree relationship.

Now add an independent warranty panel in another Lightning page region. It needs to react when the salesperson selects a different visit. Publish a small message on a new SAM_Visit_Selected__c message channel. The warranty panel subscribes and reloads authorized details, rather than trusting a payload containing customer and VIN information.

callouts.text: Would publishing this message notify a separate backend integration that is not running in the Lightning application?

codeBlocks.caption: Child event fragment; parent listens with onvisitselect
Complete SAM_Visit_Selected.messageChannel-meta.xml declaration
codeBlocks.code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<LightningMessageChannel xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
    <masterLabel>SAM Visit Selected</masterLabel>
    <isExposed>true</isExposed>
    <description>Selected training appointment identifier.</description>
    <lightningMessageFields>
        <fieldName>recordId</fieldName>
        <description>Selected Test Drive ID.</description>
    </lightningMessageFields>
</LightningMessageChannel>

sections.heading: Build and inspect
body: Create the message-channel metadata under force-app/main/default/messageChannels. Its imported schema name includes __c. No new Salesforce object or field is required.

steps.title: Build the parent-child path
steps.instruction: Dispatch a narrow selection event and handle it in the parent. Keep input ownership in the parent and avoid mutating the passed record.
steps.expected: The child works without knowing its surrounding page layout.

steps.title: Add the independent subscriber
steps.instruction: Use lightning/messageService with the declared channel, a MessageContext, and a guarded subscription. Publish only recordId and reload details through the subscriber's data source.
steps.expected: The independent panel follows selection without sharing private DOM.

steps.title: Test lifetime and scope
steps.instruction: Open, close, and revisit the page or workspace. Compare the intended active-area behavior with application scope where supported, and count handler calls.
steps.expected: One published selection causes one intended update per active subscriber.

sections.heading: Failure cases and boundaries
body: An overly broad message can make unrelated components react and create difficult-to-trace loops. Define event names and which component is authoritative for selection.
Messages are not a durable record of business completion. If the user reloads the page, recover state from the appropriate data source rather than expecting old LMS messages to replay.

callouts.text: Do not describe LMS as a durable server-side event stream or as a replacement for authorization.

exercise.title: Connect a list and an independent panel
exercise.brief: Demonstrate DOM events for one component tree and LMS for a separate panel.
steps: Deploy the message channel and subscriber.
Test duplicate subscriptions and page lifetime.
acceptance: DOM and LMS responsibilities are distinct.
Scope and cleanup behavior are explained.
exercise.stretch: Explain one limitation and propose a small follow-up experiment before extending the implementation.

knowledgeCheck.question: When is a DOM event simpler?
knowledgeCheck.answer: When a child can communicate through its ordinary parent relationship.

knowledgeCheck.question: Does LMS replace Platform Events?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. They serve different client-application and server-integration boundaries.

knowledgeCheck.question: Should the payload contain the whole customer?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Usually no. Send the minimal identity and let the subscriber read authorized current data.

recap: Use LMS for the right boundary.
